_meta.purpose: Disqualifier rules for corpus_append.py. A company classified into any of these buckets is dropped before being appended to companies.json.
_meta.philosophy: Mechanical rejection only. No scoring, no LLM, no heuristics. Either the slug or name matches a pattern or it does not. When in doubt, do not add a rule — let the JD scoring stage filter the role instead.

consumer_crypto_retail.note: Targets retail crypto trading. Does NOT target B2B crypto infrastructure (custody platforms, institutional crypto, blockchain enterprise) — those can have legitimate Joey-fit roles.

dating_apps.note: Consumer dating only. B2B matchmaking and professional networking platforms are not in scope here.

gambling.note: Gambling and sportsbook. Does NOT target gaming companies broadly (game studios, esports, etc.).

mlm_direct_sales.note: MLM is a small specific category. Names rarely match — keyword matching is the better signal.

religious_nonprofits.note: Religious nonprofits are a known disqualifier. Generic 'nonprofit' is NOT a disqualifier — many growth-stage companies are technically nonprofits.

consumer_lifestyle_apps.note: Targets consumer wellness and lifestyle. Does NOT target enterprise wellness, B2B health platforms, or healthtech with a meaningful technical product.

healthcare_admin.note: Targets healthcare admin and billing. Does NOT target healthtech, biotech, medical devices, digital health, or healthcare infrastructure.

recruiting_agencies.note: Companies whose product IS recruiting, not companies that are hiring. The job listings they post are at OTHER companies.

job_aggregators.note: Indeed, Glassdoor reposts, etc. Roles surfaced from these are the aggregator's own internal roles.

order: 3. sector_keyword_clusters: any cluster where 2+ keywords appear in name or snippet → reject
rules.rejection_audit: All rejections are logged to disqualified_<week>.csv with slug, name, rejected_by_rule, matched_keywords, and snippet. Review the log periodically to tune the lists.
